language.title: Language
language.help: The language of this window. The player page on phones and TVs follows each device’s own language.
error.title: Something went wrong
error.body: The interface hit an unexpected problem. Your server and library are not affected.
appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.help: “System” follows your computer’s setting. This choice applies to this window only.
server.title: Server
connect.title: Connect a device
connect.intro.lan: On a TV, iPad or phone on the same Wi-Fi, scan the code or open this address.
connect.intro.private: On a device signed in to your account there, scan the code or open this address. It works from anywhere.
connect.intro.public: From any browser, open this address and enter your PIN. The code opens the sign-in page; it does not contain the PIN.
connect.tokenWarning: These links include your access token. Share them only with people you trust.
connect.playlistNeedsSignIn: To play in VLC or Infuse, sign in on the player page first, then use “Playlist for VLC / Infuse” there. Its links stay valid for a few hours.
connect.noNetwork.title: No local network found
connect.noNetwork.body: Connect this computer to Wi-Fi or Ethernet, then stop and start the server so it can pick up the new address. Until then it can only be opened from this computer.
stats.title: Library
settings.startup.title: Starting up
settings.startup.intro: So your library is there when a TV or phone looks for it.
settings.startup.autoStart.title: Start sharing when EinCast opens
settings.startup.autoStart.help: The server starts by itself, so there is nothing to click before a TV can connect.
settings.startup.keepAwake.title: Keep my computer awake while sharing
settings.startup.keepAwake.help: A sleeping laptop can't be reached. The screen may still turn off. Applies the next time the server starts.
settings.startup.openAtLogin.title: Open EinCast when I sign in
settings.startup.openAtLogin.help: EinCast starts with the computer, in the background when closing the window keeps it sharing.
settings.startup.hideOnClose.title: Keep sharing when I close the window
settings.startup.hideOnClose.darwin: EinCast stays in the Dock and keeps sharing. Quit it with ⌘Q (EinCast → Quit) to stop. Takes effect the next time EinCast opens.
settings.startup.hideOnClose.windows: EinCast stays in the notification area and keeps sharing. Right-click its icon and choose Quit to stop. Takes effect the next time EinCast opens.
settings.startup.hideOnClose.fallback: EinCast keeps sharing when the window is closed. Takes effect the next time EinCast opens.
settings.network.title: Network
settings.network.intro: If a TV or phone can't see EinCast, start here.
settings.network.refreshHelp: Use this after the Wi-Fi or cable changed. It restarts the server, which also turns off remote access.
settings.network.refreshUnavailable: Available while the server is running.
settings.network.hint.same.title: Same network.
settings.network.hint.same.text: The device and this computer must be on the same Wi-Fi. A guest network usually can't see the main one.
settings.network.hint.isolation.title: Wi-Fi client isolation.
settings.network.hint.isolation.text: Some routers and mesh systems stop devices talking to each other ("AP isolation", "guest mode"). The address and QR code won't work either until it is turned off.
settings.network.hint.discovery.title: Blocked discovery.
settings.network.hint.discovery.text: A firewall or router that drops UDP ports 1900 and 5353 hides the server from TVs and from eincast.local. Typing the address still works.
settings.network.hint.firewall.title: The first-run firewall prompt.
settings.network.hint.firewall.text: macOS and Windows ask whether to allow incoming connections the first time. Choose Allow (on Windows, tick Private networks), or nothing can connect.
settings.server.title: Server
settings.server.restartNote: Saved. The running server keeps its old port and name until you stop and start it.
settings.conversion.hardware.title: Use hardware acceleration
settings.conversion.hardware.help: Converts videos with your computer's video chip: faster, and the fan stays quieter. If the chip can't do a video, EinCast uses the processor instead. Applies to the next video converted.
settings.access.title: Access token
settings.access.on: Devices need the link or QR code shown on the Dashboard. Anyone without it is turned away.
settings.access.off: Off: anyone on your Wi-Fi who knows the address can open your library.
settings.access.dlnaOn: Smart TV discovery is on, and TVs can't send a token. Turn it off below to use the token.
settings.access.recommend: Recommended: turn this on if other people use your network.
settings.access.noKeychain: The system keychain isn't available, so this token will change the next time EinCast starts.
settings.access.lockout: Devices using the old link will be locked out.
settings.tv.title: Smart TVs
settings.tv.on: Smart TVs and media players on your network find EinCast by themselves and can browse your library.
settings.tv.off: Off: TVs have to be given the address, or play the playlist from VLC or Infuse.
settings.tv.tradesToken: The access token is on, and TVs can't send it. Turning this on turns the token off.
settings.tv.dialogWarning: Smart TVs can't send the access token, so EinCast would list your library to everyone on this network, without a password. Keep the token if you share your Wi-Fi with people you don't trust, and give the TV the address instead.
settings.tv.disableToken: Turn off the token and enable Smart TVs
settings.tv.openNote: This lists your library to everyone on the same network, without a password. Use it on a home network you trust.
settings.tv.restart: Saved. Stop and start the server for this to take effect.
settings.port.title: Free a port
settings.port.intro: If the server won't start because the port is already in use, find the program holding it and end it.
settings.port.self: This is EinCast. Stop the server from the Dashboard to free the port.
settings.port.unsaved: Unsaved work in this program may be lost.
settings.ffmpeg.intro: Optional. Gives your library thumbnails and lets iPhones, iPads and TVs play MKV and HEVC videos.
settings.ffmpeg.badChoice: The ffmpeg you chose can't be used. Pick another, or let EinCast look for it.
settings.ffmpeg.missing: ffmpeg wasn't found. Without it, videos show an icon instead of a picture, and files an iPhone can't play won't play.
settings.ffmpeg.installHint: Install it by pasting this in a terminal:
settings.ffmpeg.installAfter: Then choose Check again. No restart needed.
library.manager.title: Libraries
library.manager.intro: The folders EinCast serves. Add as many as you like; one cannot contain another.
library.card.name: Library name
library.card.watching: Watching this folder: added and removed files appear by themselves.
library.card.notWatching: Changes on disk are not picked up automatically. Use Rescan after adding or removing files.
library.card.hiddenFromTVs: Kept off smart TVs. A TV can't say who is watching, so it only sees libraries that are shown to TVs.
library.card.shownToTVs: Shown to smart TVs, when Smart TVs is on. A TV can't say who is watching, so turn this off for what a child shouldn't see.
library.card.confirm: Remove “{name}” from EinCast? Your files are not touched.
library.view.installFfmpeg: Install ffmpeg (for example “brew install ffmpeg”) to see thumbnails here and on your devices.
library.sort.name: Name
onboarding.pick: Pick the folder with your videos, music and photos. EinCast will scan it so your other screens can play it.
wizard.share.running: Anything on your Wi-Fi with this code or address can open your library.
wizard.share.notRunning: EinCast serves your folder to the screens on your Wi-Fi. Nothing leaves your home.
wizard.share.tokenNote: The code includes your access token, so only devices you show it to can open the library.
wizard.share.noNetwork: No local network found. Connect to Wi-Fi or plug in a cable, then come back to Settings → Network.
wizard.connect.title: Open it on your TV or phone
wizard.connect.intro: Use whichever of these suits the screen.
wizard.connect.phoneText: point the camera at the code from the last step.
wizard.connect.tvText: open its web browser and type the address.
wizard.connect.vlcText: use the playlist link on the Dashboard.
wizard.connect.waiting: Waiting for a device to connect…
wizard.firewall.darwin: If macOS asks whether EinCast may accept incoming network connections, choose Allow. Without it, other devices can't connect.
wizard.firewall.windows: If Windows asks whether to let EinCast through the firewall, tick Private networks and choose Allow access. Without it, other devices can't connect.
wizard.firewall.fallback: If your system asks whether EinCast may accept incoming connections, allow it.
profiles.title: Profiles
profiles.introFew: Add a profile for the kids, or for anyone who should see only part of the library. Devices then choose who is watching.
profiles.introMany: A device chooses a profile when it connects. Each profile has its own “Continue watching”.
profiles.advice.one: {names} can see everything and has no PIN, so anyone can pick it to get past the others. Give it a PIN, or limit what it can see.
profiles.advice.other: {names} can see everything and has no PIN, so anyone can pick it to get past the others. Give it a PIN, or limit what it can see.
profiles.editor.name: Name
profiles.editor.allLibraries: All libraries, including ones added later
profiles.editor.noneTicked: With no library ticked, this profile sees nothing.
profiles.editor.hideHelp: Hides everything inside a folder with that name, at any depth. {star} and {question} are wildcards.
profiles.editor.pinHelp: Asked when someone picks this profile on a TV, phone or tablet. It stops a curious child, not someone who can read the files on this computer.
remote.badge.failed: Public access may still be ON
remote.provider.tailscale.summary: Private. Only devices signed in to your own Tailscale account can connect, and nothing is opened to the Internet. Install Tailscale on this computer and on the device you want to watch on.
remote.provider.cloudflareQuick.summary: Public. A random web address that works from anywhere, with no account. It changes every time you turn it on. Anyone who finds the address can reach its sign-in page, so a PIN is required. Needs the free cloudflared tool installed on this computer.
remote.provider.cloudflareNamed.summary: Public. A stable address on your own domain, through your own Cloudflare account. Anyone who finds the address can reach its sign-in page, so a PIN is required. You create the tunnel in Cloudflare first, and it needs the free cloudflared tool installed on this computer.
remote.provider.ngrok.summary: Public. A web address from your ngrok account, with nothing else to install. The free plan has a very small data allowance and shows a warning page to browsers, so it suits trying remote access, not watching films. A PIN is required.
remote.provider.cloudflareNotice: Cloudflare's service terms restrict serving large amounts of video through their proxy outside their paid video products. This is fine for light personal use; heavy streaming may violate Cloudflare's terms. Tailscale is recommended for regular remote viewing.
remote.provider.ngrokNotice: ngrok's free plan allows very little data and is meant for testing, not for streaming movies. If you go over, ngrok can stop the tunnel. Tailscale is recommended for regular remote viewing.
remote.provider.unknownPublic: Public: anyone who learns the address can reach its sign-in page. Needs an access PIN.
remote.provider.unknownPrivate: Private: only your own devices can reach it.
remote.provider.cloudflareNamedNote: In Cloudflare, the tunnel's public hostname must point at this server: set its service to {where}. If you change the port in Settings, change it there too.
remote.provider.portWhere: http://localhost and the port shown in Settings
remote.title: Remote access
remote.intro: Watch your library away from home. Pick how devices outside this network connect.
remote.noProviders: No remote access options are available in this version of EinCast.
remote.publicWarning: Anyone on the Internet who learns the address can reach its sign-in page. Only your PIN stands between them and your library.
remote.uploadNote: Playing away from home is limited by your home internet's upload speed. A film needs a few megabits per second to your viewer, all the time it plays.
remote.qrNote: The Dashboard shows a QR code for it under “Connect a device”.
remote.setup.title: Set up {label}
remote.setup.turnOffFirst: Turn {label} off to change its settings.
remote.pin.title: Access PIN
remote.pin.intro: Required for any connection that is open to the Internet. Devices enter it once to sign in. Private options such as Tailscale don't need it.
remote.pin.label: PIN
remote.pin.hint: At least 8 characters. A few random words is better than digits.
remote.pin.signsOut: Changing the PIN signs out everyone who is signed in.
remote.pin.removeBlocked: Turn off public access before removing the PIN.
remote.pin.removeBlockedShort: Turn off public access to remove it.
updates.title: Updates
updates.intro: EinCast looks on GitHub for a newer version about once a day. It only tells you: it never downloads or installs anything by itself. Nothing about you or this computer is sent.
updates.currentDev: This build was made from source and has no version number, so there is nothing to compare.
updates.auto.title: Check for updates automatically
updates.auto.help: About once a day EinCast asks GitHub for the newest release. Turn this off and it makes no request at all, unless you press “Check now”.
updates.noChecksum: No checksum was published for this file.
updates.verify: To check a download, compare its SHA-256 with the one above. On a Mac, run “shasum -a 256 <file>” in Terminal; on Windows, run “Get-FileHash <file>” in PowerShell.
